attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The proposition matches the sentence. 'Great model' is opinion, and the contract rightly leaves it unscored. The testable parts are that it led most benchmarks at launch and was not AGI.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: first on most launch benchmarks, and nobody credible calls it AGI. AGI has no agreed definition, but the contract only asks that no credible source, Google included, treated it as AGI.

evidence.note: Company disclosure from launch day: tops LMArena, HLE, GPQA and others. It calls the model a step 'on the path toward AGI', which implies it is not AGI. As a company source, its benchmark claims are not independent.
Independent launch evaluation. First on the overall index and on 5 of 10 component evals, and also first on Omniscience and MMMU-Pro. Taken together, that is a lead on most measures.
Hassabis said in Feb 2026 that AGI was not yet reached. That is three months after the target period, so it is context only, though consistent with the claim.

reviews.rationale: At launch, Gemini 3 Pro led most reported benchmarks. Google's table (e1) and the independent Artificial Analysis evaluation (e2) agree, with AA showing it first overall and on most of its listed evals. Google itself framed the model as a step toward AGI, not as AGI, and no source in the packet calls it AGI. Both testable parts hold.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'most measures' qualifier. It is a launch-time observation.

contract.note: Reading 'most measures' as a majority of the standard launch benchmarks, with at least one independent leaderboard, is a fair and ordinary reading.

evidence.note: Company disclosure: first on LMArena and top scores on HLE, GPQA, MathArena Apex and SimpleQA. Not independent.
Independent: first overall, first on 5 of 10 index evals, and also first on Omniscience and MMMU-Pro.
Launch-day news summary saying it beat Anthropic and OpenAI models on nearly all tests. It is drawn largely from Google's own table.
Claude edged it on SWE-bench Verified. One exception like this is consistent with 'most'.

reviews.rationale: Google's comparison table, a news summary of it, and the independent Artificial Analysis results all show Gemini 3 Pro first on a majority of launch measures. Exceptions such as SWE-bench, and AA's 5 of 10 component evals, fit the word 'most' and do not contradict it. Ranking first on the AA index and on extra evals supports a majority lead.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The revision keeps 'usual' and ties the timing to the announcement. It is a checkable observation about launch-day reports.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair. But the result turns on two calls Marcus did not make himself: whether one well-documented thread plus replies satisfies the plural 'reports', and whether an error partly caused by a disabled tool counts as 'silly'.

evidence.note: Article embeds Karpathy's viral thread, dated launch day, describing Gemini 3 refusing to accept the year and calling real evidence fake. It also mentions replies on X.
TechCrunch describes the same error, the model accusing the user of supplying AI-made fakes, as a telling limitation.
Search tool had been left off, which softens the error. But the model treating real evidence as fabricated is still an error.

reviews.rationale: A widely seen launch-day thread documented an embarrassing Gemini 3 error, and press coverage dates it to 18 Nov. Neither contradiction condition is met: reports did not wait days, and the failure was real. Caveats: only one report is well documented, and the disabled tool partly explains the error. Under the contract's plain reading, the claim holds.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Faithful to the claim that hallucinations and unreliability persist, as in earlier models. It does not claim there was no improvement.

contract.note: Reading 'unreliability' through hallucination rates and documented errors is a fair and ordinary reading. The contradiction condition, near-zero or solved, is matched correctly to 'persist'.

evidence.note: Independent launch-day test: 88% hallucination rate, higher than rivals'.
Reports the 88% rate as matching Gemini 2.5 models, so the tendency to hallucinate is unchanged.
Company disclosure of a 72.1% SimpleQA score. That shows progress but not that hallucination was solved, so the contradiction condition is not met.

reviews.rationale: Independent launch evaluations show Gemini 3 Pro's hallucination rate at 88%, the same as earlier Gemini models and above its rivals'. Google's reported accuracy gains do not show the problem near zero or solved. The claim that hallucinations persist holds.
